pr_title: ARM Cortex-M: Fix booting in no-multithreading mode
pr_body:
This PR fixes the issues with Cortex-M when building without multi-threading support. In particular
- it properly sets the PSP _back_ to the main stack so main() uses the main stack and ISRs will use the _interrupt_stack. This has never worked, but needs to work, in order to use IRQs in the no multi-threading case.
- configures FPU, MPU guards and PSPLIM accordingly, to mimic what is going on in the normal CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=y case. This allows to use FPU and HW stack overflow in main().
- adds the required hook in the kernel z_cstart() to make the change less intrusive; only Cortex-M is affected - no other functional cases.



I am going to add a simple test to verify the feature. **Test added**

Also this PR fixes a minor enhancement issue with the interrupt stack in reset.S.


Fixes #26796
Fixes #16210
pr_comments:

* nrf52840dk_nrf52840 (program runs, but once interrupt fires everything stops)
* frdm_k64f (program dies after BOOT_BANNER)

Clearly `CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=n` is a poorly tested configuration, and the failure is *not* Nordic-specific.

With this patch using master button test (and default `CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=y`) all platforms pass.

@andyross thanks. There are some advantages of keeping the two stacks (but I agree with you that a single stack would work too). Zephyr ARM architecture code heavily depends on the fact that the ISRs use a different stack from the thread mode; if we want to use the same stack, lots of things need to be re-worked, and I wanted to **avoid** this.

A good example is the stack overflow case (and in general, the fault handling). Assessing faults is done by inspecting the stack frame which is on PSP; if we want to use MSP in the no-multithreading case, fault inspection needs a re-write.

Also, ARM reset code uses the interrupt stack with the Process stack pointer. We don't want to modify this common code and create confusion. Since IRQs will use the Main stack pointer, we need to switch _back_ to using MSP in thread mode after initialization; this requires lots of #ifdef CONFIG_MULTITHREADING in the architecture code base.

Using a different stack pointer, depending on CONFIG_MULTITHREADING will also be a bit confusing for developers that need to debug Cortex-M code; they are used to see the main() running on PSP.

The interrupt stack gets defined in kernel code, same as the main stack, so we're reserving the area anyways, so not using it does not bring any benefit (unless we change kernel code for that, which i did not want to do). The point was to support this feature properly, with as few changes to the code base as possible.
Do not merge until the outcome of #27415 is decided.

Not sure I agree with this principle, @carlescufi. The discussion of whether to support single-threading or not is legitimate, however, this PR is a bug fix of an existing feature in zephyr, it is only a bug fix, and affects nothing outside the single-threading case. We're rapidly approaching feature freeze and need to start looking at stabilizing what we've got.  It would be bad to put this off for very long.

@ioannisg and @pabigot This introduces functionality that is strictly tied to `CONFIG_MULTITHREADING`, that was my reasoning for waiting to merge this. But since deciding on the future of that Kconfig variable might take time, I agree to merge this in the meantime.

issue_context.title: Interrupts on Cortex-M do not work with CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=n
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When `CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=n` then interrupts are initially disabled (see bug #8393) when they are enabled then usage fault happens immediately (seems that it happens during returning from interrupt).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. modify hello_world:
```
void main(void)
{
        /* enable interrupts */
	irq_unlock(0);
	printk("Hello World! %s\n", CONFIG_BOARD);
        /* wait for interrupt coming from LF clock being started. */
	k_busy_wait(1000000);

}
```

prj.conf:
```
CONFIG_MULTITHREADING=n
CONFIG_LOG=y
```

2. buid and run. I used nrf52840dk_nrf52840 board
4. See error
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.3.0-979-ga043d48c5472  ***
[00:00:02.426,116] <err> os: ***** USAGE FAULT *****
[00:00:02.426,116] <err> os:   Illegal load of EXC_RETURN into PC
[00:00:02.426,116] <err> os: r0/a1:  0x00000004  r1/a2:  0x00000001  r2/a3:  0x00000001
[00:00:02.426,116] <err> os: r3/a4:  0x00000000 r12/ip:  0x00000020 r14/lr:  0x000029db
[00:00:02.426,116] <err> os:  xpsr:  0x00000000
[00:00:02.426,147] <err> os: Faulting instruction address (r15/pc): 0xe000ed00
[00:00:02.426,147] <err> os: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 0: CPU exception on CPU 0
[00:00:02.426,147] <err> os: Current thread: 0x00000000 (unknown)
[00:00:03.378,143] <err> os: Halting system
```

**Expected behavior**
No error should appear.

**Impact**
Interrupts cannot be used when multithreading is off. User cannot use any driver (even out of tree which does not use kernel synchronization apis).

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Commit a043d48c54726082521f3e335d807dc649cc02f3

@carlescufi @de-nordic @nordic-krch This issue caught my attention and I took a quick deeper look. I think the problem lies in incorrect configuration of stack pointer registers when `CONFIG_MULTITHREADING` is disabled.
Thread mode is configured to use PSP here:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/3bc6c555a51888b5996d06f68f7b65892a9c79e2/arch/arm/core/aarch32/cortex_m/reset.S#L95-L98
Because further initialization is done this way:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/7d90812f265c0d23bad904434cef9c1616ba08ad/kernel/init.c#L475-L479
PSP is not reconfigured to the top of the main stack by this code that is called from `switch_to_main_thread()`:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/4c673395718e862949a6c153214662fbc92cd479/arch/arm/core/aarch32/thread.c#L430-L438
and after initialization is finished, PSP points to the same stack as MSP, just a little below MSP. Then, if an interrupt routine uses the stack (pointed by MSP) more intensively, it can overwrite the values stacked there on the exception entry (using PSP) and the return from exception may fail in various ways (most likely with UsageFault). But if all interrupt routines don't use too much stack, everything can work correctly for quite a long time. As @de-nordic already signaled:
> Waiting for @nordic-krch input on the 2881df3, but I am afraid that the change might have uncovered the issue rather than introduce it.

And it seems this issue may occur on all Cortex-M SoCs. I'm not sure who would be the best person to look at this problem.

review_comments:
Shouldn't the `#ifdef ARCH_SWITCH_TO_MAIN_NO_MULTITHREADING` end here, so that the execution falls into the `while (true)` loop below in case `bg_thread_main()` returns? See the end of `bg_thread_main()`:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/b8f4f2032c862979b6c0eaa28e008f1c998fb904/kernel/init.c#L261-L270.

I think this is complicated to do and might not worth the effort.
Normally, if a function changes the stack pointer, it should not return to the caller (using the caller convention). Such functions should not return. That's what happens, practically in `switch_to_main_thread(prepare_multithreading());`
Might be ok if the caller does not use the stack, but it feels _too_ error prone.
Then maybe such infinite loop should be added to `z_arm_switch_to_main_no_multithreading()` so that this function indeed cannot (try to) return?
Yes, that I could do. I'll mimic the init.c  and add an irq_lock and a while(1)
